Radial/femoral pulse deficit
HINTS exam (head impulse, nystagmus, test of skew)
Gait assessment: can the patient stand and walk unaided (sit unsupported; truncal ataxia)
Dix-Hallpike maneuver on each side, observing latency, duration, and direction of nystagmus
Ask about known COPD diagnosis or prior spirometry, home inhalers, and prior exacerbations needing steroids or intubation
Forced expiratory time (timed forced exhalation, >=9 s)

Calf circumference asymmetry >3 cm (10 cm below tibial tuberosity)
Wells DVT items on history and exam: bedridden >3 days, active cancer, prior VTE, recent surgery, pitting edema confined to the symptomatic leg, collateral superficial veins
Inspect surgical wound for erythema, warmth, drainage, dehiscence, and tenderness beyond the incision
Costovertebral angle (CVA) tenderness and suprapubic tenderness
Cardiac auscultation for a new or changed murmur
Capillary refill time (>3 s), skin mottling over the knees, cool extremities
Mental status and respiratory rate at the bedside (qSOFA elements)
Ask about melena, hematemesis, and hematochezia
JVP (jugular venous pressure)
Bedside hemodynamic stability: mentation, chest pain, dyspnea, Capillary refill time, skin temperature
Cannon a waves in the jugular venous pulse and variable intensity of S1 (AV dissociation)
Dynamic auscultation: murmur intensity with Valsalva and squat-to-stand (louder with Valsalva or standing suggests HCM, softer suggests AS)
Dry axilla / mucous membranes
Witness account: duration, color, jerking, tongue biting, incontinence, post-event confusion (from nurse)
Establish last-known-well time precisely
Ask: focal versus generalized, sudden versus gradual onset, new today or progressive since admission, and whether the problem is weakness, dizziness, or pain on standing
Proximal strength: sit-to-stand without arms, hip flexion against resistance, arms held above head
